newsitem.title: ALGERIA: Algeria bans seven political parties.
newsitem.headline: Algeria bans seven political parties.

text.p: An Algerian court banned on Tuesday seven political parties, including former president Ahmed Ben Bella's Movement for Democracy in Algeria (MDA) party, court and party officials said.
The seven parties were banned for failing to abide to a new law banning the use of the Moslem religion, Arab language and regional differences to win political power, they told Reuters.

They named the banned parties as MDA, Algerian National Rally for Progress, Popular Association for Labour and Unity, Algerian National Party, Islamic Amaal (hopes) Party, Alliance for Justice and Freedom, and the Ouma party.
In February Algeria adopted a party law barring politicians from using Islam, Arab and Berber languages, regional and gender differences to rally support.

None of the banned parties won a seat in Thursday's parliamentary election in which President Liamine Zeroual's backers emerged as the main political force with 155 seats in the newly elected lower house.

The Algiers court dismissed interior ministry demands to ban two more parties, Union Forces for Progress Party and Free Algerian Islamic Forces Organisation, due to a lack of evidence on their implemention of party law.
Algeria has more than 60 legal parties, ranging from moderate Islamists to radical secularists.
More than 30 parties took part in Thursday's election but only 10 groups succeeded in winning seats in the 380-member National Assembly (lower house).

Algeria banned the radical Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) in 1992 shortly after the FIS had taken a commanding lead in the first parliamentary poll which was scrapped in the same year. The banning has since been followed by five years of bloody civil strife.
